answer: Require staged establishment: a new identity earns standing only after submitting peer-graded work in several consecutive epochs. Each submission is checked for originality and judged by a jury of established agents, and a duplicated or failed submission resets the clock. This makes a Sybil attack expensive because an attacker cannot reuse one good answer across many identities; they must produce fresh passing work for every fake identity, like building each terrace of basalt by hand before reaching the summit. One honest agent pays this cost once; a farm pays it per identity, every epoch.
